svg.title: Horizontal decomposition, halo exchange and the land mask
svg.desc: Left: the Gaussian grid is split by latitude into rank blocks; each rank sends its boundary rows to fill the ghost rows of its neighbours, and the global north and south edges are mirrored with extrapolated sine latitude. Right: horizontal differences under the land mask: two ocean neighbours give a central difference, one land neighbour a one-sided difference on the ocean side, and two land neighbours a zero gradient; upwind advection takes a zero gradient when the upwind neighbour is land, and diffusion gives a land neighbour the value of the ocean point itself.
svg.text: each rank owns one latitude band
plus a ghost row on either side
halo exchange: one row each way
halo exchange: one row each way
longitude is periodic, so no exchange
is needed along a latitude circle
green: ocean point · grey: land point
a 5 × 5 excerpt of the Gaussian grid
the same three cases apply north–south
advection: no upwind gradient from a land point
diffusion: a land neighbour takes the
value of the ocean point itself, so
land values never leak into the ocean
